chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them).

Regarding a man who divorces his wife with a divorce in which he retains the right of reversion, then he dies while she is in her waiting period, he said: She observes the waiting period of the longer of the two terms, four months and ten days.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman whose husband dies after divorcing her revocably?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, where the woman remains in a state of uncertainty until the longer period elapses to ensure the validity of her marital status. The Imam's decision to prioritize the waiting period for death (four months and ten days) over the divorce period (three months) prevents any ambiguity regarding potential pregnancy or the finality of the divorce. This specific case illustrates the nuanced interaction between the two distinct types of 'iddah' when they overlap due to the husband's death during the revocable phase.
